result: Wave 1 follicles develop in the ovarian medulla without entering dormancy, while wave 2 follicles form primordial follicles in the cortex. At P5 and P10, approximately 3822 and 3304 total follicles per ovary were counted, with 278 and 293 wave 1 follicles, respectively. The number of wave 1 follicles remained relatively consistent despite variations in total follicle numbers.
evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C16, C17, C39, C40, and C41 are well-supported by quantitative data from whole-mount imaging and follicle counting using Imaris software (Figure 1C-F, Table 1). The consistency of wave 1 follicle numbers across samples strengthens the reliability of these measurements. The claims are consistent with cited literature and the experimental approach is appropriate.

result: Wave 1 follicles reach preantral stages containing theca cell layers by 2 weeks, develop into secondary follicles with 2-4 layers of granulosa cells and 1-2 layers of theca cells, and by 3 weeks some develop into antral follicles. Oocyte volume increased significantly from 1 to 3 weeks (p < 0.0001).
evaluation: Claims C4, C42, C43, and C44 are supported by imaging data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-D) and quantitative analysis using Imaris surface modeling (Figure 1G-H). The significant increase in oocyte volume is statistically validated with appropriate p-values. The developmental progression is well-documented with visual and quantitative evidence.

result: Atresia of wave 1 follicles begins around 3 weeks, with 80-100% of follicles degrading their oocytes by 5 weeks. During atresia, microvilli retract from the zona pellucida, which folds as the cavity shrinks. ZP remnants serve as morphological indicators of atresia. These findings were confirmed in both C57BL/6J and DBA/2J strains.
evaluation: Claims C5, C6, C45-C51 are supported by quantitative data showing oocyte loss (Figure 1J), electron microscopy revealing ultrastructural changes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), and validation in multiple mouse strains (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B). The temporal progression is well-documented with statistical significance (p < 0.01, p < 0.0001). The use of multiple strains strengthens the generalizability of findings.

result: Wave 1 follicles turn over 94% of their granulosa cells during atresia but retain theca cells. At 2 weeks, 201 preantral wave 1 follicles (90% of wave 1 follicles) exhibited mosaic EYFP labeling in granulosa cells. By 5 weeks, only 26 antral follicles with healthy oocytes and EYFP-mosaic granulosa cells remained. Approximately 80% of remodeled follicles retained some labeled granulosa cells that continued to express Foxl2.
evaluation: Claims C7, C52-C56 are supported by lineage tracing experiments using Foxl2-CreERT2 with quantitative analysis (Figure 2E-I). The 94% granulosa cell loss is statistically significant (p < 0.0001, Figure 2G). The persistence of Foxl2 expression in remnant granulosa cells is demonstrated by TAM injection at 5 weeks (Figure 2I). The experimental design appropriately uses mosaic labeling to track cell fate.

result: Theca cells expand in number together with interstitial gland cells in the medulla during wave 1 atresia. Between 2 and 5 weeks, tdTomato-labeled cells associated with follicular cavities increased dramatically. By 5 weeks, atretic wave 1 follicles generated a cellular cluster in the medulla dominated by steroidogenic cells displaying distinctive lipid droplets and mitochondria, which persisted until at least 7 weeks.
evaluation: Claims C8, C62-C66 are supported by Cyp17a1 lineage tracing (Figure 4D-E), electron microscopy showing steroidogenic cell ultrastructure (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), and 3D reconstruction using Imaris (Figure 4J). The inference that tdTomato-positive cells represent theca and interstitial gland cells is justified by the >90% granulosa cell turnover. The persistence of the structure is documented through 7 weeks (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).

result: During puberty (5 weeks), wave 1-derived cells ultrastructurally resemble steroidogenic cells and highly express androgen biosynthetic genes. Cluster c16 highly expressed theca cell steroidogenic genes (Cyp11a1, Cyp17a1, Plin1) and peaked at 5 weeks. The percentage of steroidogenic cells expressing Star increased from ~50% to >80% at 5 weeks. Granulosa cells expressing estrogen biosynthetic genes peaked at 6 weeks.
evaluation: Claims C9, C10, C69, C70, C74-C76 are supported by electron microscopy (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), scRNA-seq data showing steroidogenic gene expression (Figure 6G-H), and temporal analysis of cell populations (Source data 6). The timing of androgen production preceding estrogen production is consistent with cited literature (Galas et al., 2012; Trova et al., 2021). The comprehensive molecular and ultrastructural characterization provides strong evidence.

result: The Foxl2 lineage tag marked about 400 primordial follicles (7% of total) located near the medullary-cortical boundary at 2 weeks. These 'boundary' or 'wave 1.5' follicles become the earliest activated wave 2 follicles, accounting for nearly 70% of secondary follicles at 5 weeks and generating 70-100% of the earliest mature oocytes. Applying Poisson distribution analysis suggested 90% of boundary follicles were detected.
evaluation: Claims C11-C13, C30-C31, C57-C61 are supported by quantitative lineage tracing data (Figure 3B, D) showing 421 ± 74 labeled primordial follicles at 2 weeks and 70% of secondary follicles labeled at 5 weeks. The Poisson distribution analysis (C58) provides statistical justification for detection efficiency. The correspondence to previously described 'poised' primordial follicles (Meinsohn et al., 2021a,b) is appropriately noted. The dramatic increase from 7% to 70% strongly supports preferential activation.

result: Fewer than 26 wave 1 follicles with oocytes survive to puberty (5 weeks), accounting for approximately 70% of all antral follicles at that stage. The contribution of wave 1 follicles to fertility is at most minor, with early-activated wave 2 boundary follicles largely responsible for early fertility.
evaluation: Claims C14, C32, C53, C82, C83 are supported by quantitative data showing only 26 antral follicles with EYFP-mosaic granulosa cells at 5 weeks (Figure 2D-F). The inference that boundary follicles, not wave 1 follicles, are responsible for early fertility is logically derived from the quantitative data showing boundary follicles account for 70% of developing follicles. This reinterprets previous findings (Zheng et al., 2014a) with new evidence.

result: Granulosa cells of antral wave 1 and 2 follicles differentially express multiple genes. Wave 1 follicles express much higher levels of Wnt4 (4.8 ± 1.0 vs 0.17 ± 0.069 at 5 weeks) and Igfbp5 (27 ± 10 fold higher) than wave 2 follicles. Nr5a2 expression is 7.8-fold higher in wave 1 BPGs at P5 but reaches similar levels in wave 1 and 2 antral follicles (ratio = 1.02 ± 0.23).
evaluation: Claims C15, C93-C94, C117-C123 are supported by scRNA-seq data comparing gene expression between wave 1 (2 weeks) and wave 2 (5-6 weeks) antral follicles. The differential expression ratios are quantified with standard deviations. The finding that Nr5a2 differences present at P5 (Niu and Spradling, 2020) converge by the antral stage, while other genes remain differentially expressed, is well-documented. This challenges the assumption that wave 1 and 2 follicles are equivalent at the same developmental stage.

result: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified 31 initial clusters with 9 major cell groups based on marker gene expression. Pseudotime trajectory analysis using Monocle 3 identified distinct developmental paths from primordial follicles: path 1 leads to antral follicles, while path 2 results in remodeled follicles.
evaluation: Claims C67-C68, C72-C73 are supported by scRNA-seq analysis with appropriate clustering (Figure 5A-D) and trajectory analysis (Figure 6D). The identification of two distinct developmental paths from the secondary stage is a key finding. The methods are standard for scRNA-seq analysis, though the manuscript could benefit from more detail on quality control metrics and batch effect correction.

result: Clusters corresponding to endothelial cells (c22) and blood cells (c23) increased nearly fourfold between 3 and 5 weeks. Granulosa cell clusters gc0 and gc6, associated with remodeling follicles, increased 9.8-fold at 4 weeks and preferentially expressed genes including Cyp1b1, Atf3, Cxcl1, Bmp2, Apoe, and Sox4. Metascape analysis identified enrichment for vasculature development, cell cycle, and programmed cell death pathways.
evaluation: Claims C71, C124-C126 are supported by scRNA-seq data (Source data 6) and Metascape pathway analysis. The fourfold increase in endothelial and blood cells is consistent with vascularization during follicle remodeling. The inference that gc0 and gc6 represent remodeling follicles is supported by their temporal appearance (low at 2-3 weeks, high at 4 weeks) and gene expression profile. The pathway analysis appropriately identifies biological processes consistent with follicle remodeling.

result: No meaningful expression level of follicle-stimulating hormone receptor (Fshr) was observed across cell types and samples during the 2-6 week period.
evaluation: Claim C77 is supported by expression data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A. This finding is consistent with the juvenile developmental stage studied (2-6 weeks), which precedes the onset of mature hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activity. The absence of Fshr expression supports the interpretation that follicle development during this period is largely gonadotropin-independent.

result: Wave 1 follicles retain early-arising bipotential pre-granulosa (BPG) cells expressing Foxl2 and Nr5a2 from early fetal development, while wave 2 follicles acquire epithelial pre-granulosa (EPG) cells and express Foxl2 only after birth. A small subset of primordial follicles express Nr5a2 and are primed for activation. Most wave 1 follicles undergo atresia after reaching early antral stages, though they can develop into functional oocytes following superovulation. Theca cells of atretic follicles often survive and persist.
evaluation: Claims C18-C29 summarize established knowledge from the literature, appropriately cited (Mork et al., 2012; Zheng et al., 2014a,b; Niu and Spradling, 2020; Meinsohn et al., 2021a,b; Byskov, 1974; Erickson et al., 1985; Lamas et al., 2021; Magoffin, 2005). These claims provide essential background context for the current study. The citations appear accurate and the claims are consistent with the field's understanding.

result: Most of the Foxl2-CreERT2-labeled follicles contributing to offspring observed by Zheng et al., 2014a likely derived from boundary follicles rather than from wave 1 follicles. Boundary primordial follicles activate as early as 2 weeks and produce most of the first follicles to develop fully, ovulate, and generate offspring.
evaluation: Claims C34, C80-C81 represent a reinterpretation of previous findings (Zheng et al., 2014a) based on the discovery of boundary follicles. The inference is logically supported by the data showing boundary follicles account for 70% of developing follicles at 5 weeks while only 26 wave 1 follicles survive. This reinterpretation is appropriately cautious, acknowledging that the previous study used the same lineage tracing approach but did not distinguish boundary follicles from wave 1 follicles.

result: In agreement with earlier studies, 80-100% of wave 1 follicles turn over rather than generating fertilizable oocytes. Wave 1 follicles play a role in steroid production during juvenile development, especially at puberty.
evaluation: Claims C78-C79 are supported by the quantitative data on oocyte loss (Figure 1J) and the comprehensive characterization of steroidogenic cell expansion and gene expression (Figures 4, 6G). The agreement with earlier studies (Hirshfield and DeSanti, 1995; Gougeon, 1996; McGee and Hsueh, 2000) strengthens the findings. The proposed steroidogenic role is well-supported by molecular and ultrastructural evidence.

result: Most non-boundary wave 2 follicles may begin to activate between puberty and sexual maturity, possibly in concert with pulsatile hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activity. Boundary follicles may become poised to activate due to proximity to the nutrient-rich medulla. High Wnt4 expression in wave 1 granulosa cells may promote subsequent androgen upregulation at puberty through Wnt4-mediated downregulation becoming reduced by granulosa cell degradation. Wave 1-generated steroid production may influence sexual development.
evaluation: Claims C84, C91, C96, C99, C101, C114 are speculative interpretations of the data. While the speculation is reasonable and consistent with the findings, these claims lack direct experimental validation. The manuscript appropriately presents these as hypotheses rather than established facts. Additional experiments would be needed to test these mechanistic proposals, such as manipulating Wnt4 levels or measuring systemic androgen levels.

result: Early waves of germ cells with distinct developmental fates are observed across species (C. elegans, Drosophila, mouse testis). In humans, 4-6% of follicles progress to primary stage before birth, and juvenile ovaries contain 2-13% of small growing follicles with 50-60% showing signs of atresia. Wnt4 is linked to Müllerian dysgenesis and hyperandrogenism in humans. Turner syndrome shows reduced wave 1 follicle development, and hormone replacement therapy (including androgens) improves development. Peri-puberty is associated with sexual behavior development and high androgen levels. Some histological characteristics of remodeling mouse wave 1 follicles resemble PCOS follicles.
evaluation: Claims C85-C90, C95, C97, C104-C106, C110-C113, C115-C116 are appropriately cited from the literature (Pazdernik and Schedl, 2013; Lei and Spradling, 2013; Zhu and Xie, 2003; Forabosco and Sforza, 2007; Himelstein-Braw et al., 1976; Choussein et al., 2017; Schneider et al., 2002; Miura et al., 2017; Klein et al., 2018; Zuckerman-Levin et al., 2009; Viuff et al., 2022; François et al., 2017; Trova et al., 2021; Devillers et al., 2023; Erickson et al., 1985; Magoffin, 2005; Chang, 2007; Franks and Hardy, 2010; Walters et al., 2019). These claims provide important comparative and clinical context for the findings.

result: Boundary follicles appear to correspond to the primordial follicle subclass poised for early activation described by Meinsohn et al., 2021a,b. While changing gonadotropin levels likely play a role in wave 1 atresia, intrinsic gene expression differences exist and may be important. Wave 1 granulosa cells differentially express growth-promoting genes (Igfbp5, Grb14, Ghr) and signaling genes (Itga6, Inha). Follicle groups form at times overlapping with critical gonad development events. Wave 1 and boundary follicles can be preferentially marked using Foxl2-CreERT2 as early as E14.5.
evaluation: Claims C92, C98, C100, C102-C103 are supported by the correspondence in location and properties to previously described follicles (Meinsohn et al., 2021a,b), scRNA-seq data showing differential gene expression, and lineage tracing data showing early specification (Figure 3C). The inference that intrinsic gene expression differences may contribute to distinct fates is reasonable given the data, though the relative contributions of intrinsic vs. extrinsic factors remain to be determined.

result: In XO mice, activated follicle numbers were reduced compared to XX controls at 1 week, but by 2 weeks the statistical difference was no longer observed.
evaluation: Claims C107-C108 are supported by quantitative data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B-C showing significant differences at 1 week (p < 0.01) but not at 2 weeks. However, the transient nature of the phenotype limits the ability to draw conclusions about the functional role of wave 1 follicles in this genetic model. The authors appropriately acknowledge this limitation in the discussion.

result: Wave 1-derived theca cell numbers are high during 4 and 5 weeks of juvenile development, a period known as peri-puberty that has been associated with sexual behavior development and high levels of androgens.
evaluation: Claim C109 is supported by lineage tracing data showing peak theca cell numbers at 4-5 weeks (Figure 4D-E) and scRNA-seq data showing peak steroidogenic gene expression at 5 weeks (Figure 6G). The association with peri-puberty and sexual behavior development is appropriately cited (François et al., 2017; Trova et al., 2021; Devillers et al., 2023). The temporal correlation is strong, though causality is not established.
